diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recall from \cref{th:circulant_decomposition} that the Discrete Fourier Transform of each cycle of matrix provides us a circulant component.

issues.failure_explanation: With cycles of A stored as columns of \tilde A, column k of W\tilde A is the full spectrum of the single cycle k (indexed by frequency). By the paper's own proof, R_k = \sum_j r_{j,k} C^j (up to the phase \omega^{jk} from commuting D^k past C^j) collects the k-th frequency of every cycle, i.e. the k-th ROW of W\tilde A, not its k-th column. For n=2, A=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_1 C with \Lambda_0=diag(a,b), \Lambda_1=diag(c,d): the first column of R_0 is ((a+b)/2,(c+d)/2) = row 0 of the cycle-FFT, whereas column 0 gives (a+b, a-b). The phase factor is also of the wrong sign: since D^kC^j = \omega^{jk}C^jD^k, the first column of R_k is D^k (not (D^k)^{-1}) times the k-th frequency vector.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace U^{(j)} by the j-th row of U (transposed) and use the correct phase (first column of R_j = D^{j} U_{(j)}^T with proper FFT normalization); correct the prose that the DFT of a single cycle yields a circulant component.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Algorithm 2 (and the accompanying prose) does not return the circulant components R_k of Theorem th:circulant_decomposition, so Step 1–4 of Algorithm 3 build wrong truncations \tilde A, \tilde B and residues; the reported cost and the numerical results are unaffected only if a correct implementation was actually used.
issues.title: Circulant-component extraction uses the wrong column/row of the cycle-FFT matrix
issues.why_classification: A local index/phase correction restores the algorithm; the O(n^2 log n) cost and all theorems are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: W\bm l_k \circ W(D^k\bm b) = W \bm l_k \circ WD^kW^{*}W\bm b =  W\bm l_k \circ C^kW\bm b

issues.failure_explanation: W R_t D^t B = (W R_t W^*)(W D^t B) = diag(\sqrt{n}\, W\bm l_t)\, C^t W B, where \bm l_t is the first column of R_t; the paper's own derivation says the Hadamard multiplier is W\bm l_t. But L_A[t] as output by Algorithm 2 is \Lambda_t, the t-th cycle diagonal of A, which is unrelated to the eigenvalues of R_{A_t}. Hence Step 5 does not compute \tilde A B or \Delta A \tilde B (and the second line similarly uses the wrong multiplier and mixes row/column transforms).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L_A[t], L_B[t] in Step 5 by diag(FFT(R_A[t])), diag(FFT(R_B[t])) (O(n log n) each), and use a row FFT/IFFT for the \Delta A \tilde B term.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 3 as written does not deliver its stated output \tilde A B + \Delta A \tilde B; the complexity argument in the surrounding text is unaffected once the multiplier is corrected.
issues.title: Fourier-domain multiplication uses cycle diagonals \Lambda_t instead of the eigenvalues of the circulant components
issues.why_classification: Local substitution of the correct diagonal factor fixes the procedure with no change in scaling or claims.

issues.failure_explanation: With L = 2\|D_1\|_F^2\|D_2\|_2^2, 24L^2 = 96\|D_1\|_F^4\|D_2\|_2^4, which is what the proof derives in eq. (concentration). The corollary's statement uses 48, i.e. a bound smaller by a factor exp(-(n-2)t^2/96\cdots) that is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 48 by 96 in the corollary statement.
issues.overall_effect: The stated tail bound is unsupported by a factor of 2 in the exponent; qualitative use of the corollary in Proposition th:estimated_relative_error is unaffected.
issues.title: Concentration corollary states a constant (48) stronger than what its proof yields (96)
issues.why_classification: A constant correction with no loss of the qualitative concentration conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof computes E‖AB‖_F^2 /(E‖A‖_F^2 E‖B‖_F^2) = (1/9+(n-1)/16)/(n/9), which equals 9/16 only asymptotically, then replaces E‖AB‖_F by (E‖AB‖_F^2)^{1/2} and E‖A‖_F^2 by the random quantity ‖A‖_F^2 without justification. The stated exact equality is false for finite n: for n=1, ‖AB‖_F = ‖A‖_F‖B‖_F identically, so E‖AB‖_F = E[‖A‖_F‖B‖_F], not 3/4 of it.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as E‖AB‖_F^2 = (n a^4/9 + n(n-1)a^4/16)·mp exactly, with E‖AB‖_F ≈ (3/4)‖A‖_F‖B‖_F for n ≫ 1 under concentration of the norms.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem holds only as a large-n approximation (and only in the sense of concentrated norms); Proposition th:estimated_relative_error Case-2 already treats it as an approximation, so the heuristic use survives.

issues.why_classification: Weakening the statement to the asymptotic approximation the proof actually gives preserves all downstream uses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The generated matrices have singular vectors that are  orthogonal matrices with a Haar distribution

issues.failure_explanation: The value E[|Q_{ij}|^2|Q_{kl}|^2] = 1/(n(n+1)) is only correct (for Haar unitary Q) when the two entries share a row or column; for i≠k and j≠l the correct value is 1/(n^2-1), and for real orthogonal Q (the case actually generated in Appendix C) all constants differ (e.g. E[Q_{ij}^4]=3/(n(n+2))). The claimed moments are inconsistent: summing over all i,j,k,l must give E‖Q‖_F^4 = n^2, but the paper's values give (n^3+n)/(n+1). Concretely, for D_1=D_2=I, S=n deterministically so E[S^2]=n^2, whereas the lemma gives (n^2+n^4)/(n(n+1)) ≠ n^2, and Lemma lem:added-2 gives Var(S) = (n^2-n^3)/(n(n+1)) < 0.

failure_location.quote: Now using the fact that for Haar distributed matrices we have $\mathbf{E}[|Q_{i,j}|^4]  = \frac{2}{n(n+1)}$ and $\mathbf{E}[|Q_{i,j}|^2 |Q_{k,l}|^2]  = \frac{1}{n(n+1)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute E[S^2] with the correct Weingarten fourth moments (separating the cases same row, same column, distinct row and column, and real-orthogonal vs unitary), then rederive Var(S) and the E[√S] expansion.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:added-1, Lemma lem:added-2 and the subsequent Taylor-expansion formula for E[√S] in Appendix B are incorrect; the main-text heuristic 'Var → 0' used in Proposition th:estimated_relative_error loses its quantitative backing.
issues.title: Second moment of S=‖AB‖_F^2 uses incorrect Haar fourth-moment values, yielding a false E[S^2] and a negative variance
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial recomputation with different case structure is required; the resulting formulas change but a comparable variance estimate can be recovered, and only the appendix chain depends on it.
